Article 19 of Ukraine's Law on the Legal Regime of Martial Law prohibits national elections while martial law remains in effect.

How exactly is Ukraine supposed to hold free, fair and secure elections?

text:
From Ancestral Legacy to Global Recognition: The Inspiring Journey of National Awardee Shri M. Farooq Khan and AL TASVEER ART & CRAFTS

Preserving India’s Metal Craft Heritage Through Generations of Artistic Excellence, Entrepreneurship and International Trade

India’s handicraft heritage is not merely a reflection of artistic excellence but also a living testimony to generations of dedication, inherited skills, cultural identity and entrepreneurship. One such inspiring story is that of Shri M. Farooq Khan, National Awardee (2007), a distinguished metal engraving artisan, entrepreneur and exporter who has successfully transformed his ancestral craftsmanship into an internationally recognised business while preserving his family’s artistic legacy.

The foundation of this remarkable journey was laid by his grandfather, Shri Rafi Muhammad, a State Awardee, and subsequently strengthened by his father, Shri Haji Nasiruddin, recipient of the National Award in 1998 and the prestigious Shilp Guru Award in 2007. Their extraordinary contributions to traditional metal craftsmanship received recognition from the Government of India. Carrying forward this distinguished heritage, Shri Farooq Khan, together with his brothers, Shri Mohd Yusuf, National Awardee (2007), and Shri Mohd Yaqub, National Awardee (2015), continues to uphold the family’s artistic excellence.

What makes Shri Farooq Khan’s journey particularly inspiring is his educational background. Having pursued a https://t.co/eMxJbRuKD7. from Delhi University and management education at Symbiosis, Pune, he possessed opportunities to establish a professional career in India or abroad. However, his emotional attachment to ancestral craftsmanship and responsibility towards preserving traditional knowledge encouraged him to choose entrepreneurship in the handicrafts sector over a conventional corporate career.

Recognising the importance of professional identity, branding and international market confidence, the brothers established M/s AL TASVEER ART & CRAFTS, with its registered office at S-33/6, Street No. 24, Main Road, Brahampuri, Delhi–110053. The enterprise specialises in exquisite handcrafted metal engraving products, combining traditional motifs with contemporary designs, refined finishing and utilitarian applications suited to domestic and international markets.

Every creation reflects patience, precision, creativity and the artistic expression of skilled hands. Through continuous market research and exposure to international exhibitions, the enterprise has successfully adapted its products to changing consumer preferences without compromising traditional craftsmanship.

Beyond commercial achievements, the enterprise contributes significantly to artisan livelihoods. More than ten skilled artisans are associated with the establishment, receiving employment opportunities and contributing to the timely execution of orders from corporate clients, exporters and international buyers. While the brothers collectively supervise production and quality, Shri Farooq Khan primarily manages marketing, buyer coordination, export opportunities and business development, effectively applying his educational knowledge to traditional enterprise management.

The firm has reportedly achieved business turnover running into crores of rupees during recent years. According to Shri Farooq Khan, its annual export potential could exceed USD 200,000, subject to sufficient international orders, working capital and production support.

An important milestone was its participation in an international trade fair in Thessaloniki, Greece, in 2025, under the sponsorship of the Office of the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts), Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, where the enterprise received encouraging responses and orders from international buyers.

Such initiatives demonstrate how government-supported international marketing opportunities can empower award-winning artisans, establish direct buyer relationships and strengthen India’s presence in global handicraft markets. However, increasing international competition and changing procurement practices underline the need for continued overseas exposure, financial assistance and targeted marketing support for deserving artisans and enterprises.

International exhibitions offer more than commercial opportunities. They serve as platforms for cultural diplomacy, employment generation, foreign exchange earnings and the promotion of India’s traditional identity. Encouraging capable artisan entrepreneurs can therefore contribute meaningfully to the national vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and economic development.

Continuing this successful journey, M/s AL TASVEER ART & CRAFTS is participating in the 62nd IHGF Delhi Fair–Autumn 2026, showcasing its exclusive handcrafted metal artefacts before national and international buyers.

The journey of Shri M. Farooq Khan and his brothers conveys a powerful message: traditional craftsmanship, when supported by education, innovation, entrepreneurship and appropriate government initiatives, can evolve into a globally competitive enterprise.

Their story proves that preserving ancestral heritage is not merely about honouring the past; it is about creating livelihoods, expanding international markets and building a stronger India through the extraordinary skills of its artisans.

text:
The Government of India holds 55% of SBI, 97% of LIC, and 85% of IRFC. Across 73 listed companies, those stakes were worth ₹38.8 lakh crore at end-March 2026 prices.

HOW TO READ IT
Each stack of files is one company. The taller the stack, the bigger the rupee value of the government's shares in that company. The 10 tallest stacks out of 73 are shown.

WHAT STANDS OUT
- LIC at 96.5% is the most-owned by share count, yet SBI's stake is worth more: ₹4.98 lakh crore vs LIC's ₹4.43 lakh crore.
- IRFC at 85% is far more government-owned than SBI at 55%, but IRFC's stake is worth only ₹96,497 crore, about one-fifth of SBI's.
- Coal India at 63% sits between SBI and LIC, yet its ₹1.75 lakh crore is smaller than ONGC's ₹2.11 lakh crore despite ONGC's lower 59%.

HOW IT IS MEASURED
This counts the shares the Government of India holds in its own name (filed as the President of India or the Government of India), as each company filed them for 31 March 2026: its own shares in 68 companies it runs, and its stakes in 5 more that it does not run on its own (Hindustan Zinc, Vodafone Idea, IDBI Bank, IDFC First Bank, ICICI Bank). Each holding is valued at the company's last share price on or before 31 March 2026 (30 March 2026): the number of shares the government held times that price. LIC later issued bonus shares (free extra shares to every shareholder), and the price history we hold has been adjusted for it, so the price is scaled back to the shares as they were on 31 March 2026. Shares held through other government companies (HPCL through ONGC, REC through PFC, NTPC Green through NTPC, the Coal India companies), through LIC or other government-run investors, and shares held by state governments are not counted. For banks and insurers the stake is checked against the share the bank or insurer reports in its own quarterly results; for the other companies on the shelves, against the government's share count (or, where the scan is unreadable, its percentage) printed in a document the company filed. Left out: SJVN and MOIL, where the government shares the owner's seat with a state government or another investor, and its own part is not in the filings we hold; Balmer Lawrie Investments, with no share price in the month before 31 March 2026. FACT and Madras Fertilizers have no shareholding filing in our records and are not counted. Each file is ₹50,000 crore; the top file of a stack is cut to size. This is the market price of the shares on that day, not money the government could take out: selling this many shares would move the price. It is not advice.

THE 10 BIGGEST HOLDINGS
1. SBI: ₹4.98 lakh crore (government owns 55%)
2. LIC: ₹4.43 lakh crore (government owns 96.5%)
3. ONGC: ₹2.11 lakh crore (government owns 59%)
4. NTPC: ₹1.84 lakh crore (government owns 51%)
5. Coal India: ₹1.75 lakh crore (government owns 63%)
6. HAL: ₹1.67 lakh crore (government owns 72%)
7. BEL: ₹1.50 lakh crore (government owns 51%)
8. Power Grid: ₹1.41 lakh crore (government owns 51%)
9. Indian Oil: ₹98,466 crore (government owns 51.5%)
10. IRFC: ₹96,497 crore (government owns 85%)

The 10 together: ₹21.6 lakh crore. The other 63 companies: ₹17.2 lakh crore. Without SBI, the biggest, the total is ₹33.9 lakh crore.

Since 31 March 2026 the government has offered part of its shares for sale in LIC, Coal India, IRFC, Indian Overseas Bank, GIC Re, NHPC, BHEL, Hindustan Copper, NLC India and Cochin Shipyard (the companies' own filings), so some of these stakes are smaller today.

What this is: the government's own shareholdings as the companies filed them, valued at the market price. It counts companies the government runs and stakes it holds as an investor. It does not count shares held through LIC or other government companies, or by state governments.
What it is not: money the government could take out at that price (selling this many shares would move the price), and not advice.

We report filings. Not advice.

Outcomes, not selective 1940s quotes, are the clearest measure.

text:
Peshawar: 21 children, female teacher killed as private school roof collapses; dozens injured
More than 40 people, including students, were pulled from the rubble and shifted to hospital; rescue operation continues
PESHAWAR: At least 22 people, including 21 children and a female teacher, were killed and more than 40 others injured after the roof of a private school collapsed in Dir Colony, Peshawar.
According to Rescue 1122, several students were trapped under the debris after the roof of the Al-Khair School System collapsed. Ambulances and disaster-response vehicles reached the site and began rescue operations.
Later, rescue officials shifted more than 40 injured students and teachers to Lady Reading Hospital, where an emergency was declared.
Hospital administration confirmed the deaths of 21 children and a female teacher. According to the hospital spokesperson, the deceased children were aged up to 13 years, while the condition of some injured persons remained critical.
Officials said the search and rescue operation was continuing over fears that more people could be trapped under the rubble. Pakistan Army personnel and other rescue organisations are also taking part in the operation.
PM, governor express grief
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed deep sorrow over the incident, offered condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured. He directed the authorities to provide all possible medical assistance to the injured.
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also expressed grief over the tragedy, directed the relevant officials to ensure the best medical facilities for the injured and sought a detailed report on the incident.

text:
No, her framing is not credible as a straightforward account of what happened.
Nancy Pelosi did make essentially that claim (on the fifth anniversary in early 2026 and in similar remarks): she and others “begged” Trump for over three hours to send the National Guard, he never did, and he “took joy” in it / was “savoring” the situation. Contemporary records, timelines, testimony, and footage do not support the implication that Trump was the sole obstacle or that Congress/Pelosi were purely helpless victims of his refusal.
Key established points

Command authority: The Speaker of the House does not control the D.C. National Guard. Only the President, Secretary of Defense, and Secretary of the Army can authorize its deployment. Pelosi (or McConnell) could not “block” a presidential order, and they do not run Capitol security day-to-day—the Capitol Police Board does.
Before January 6: Capitol Police Chief Steven Sund requested National Guard support days earlier. The Capitol Police Board (whose House sergeant-at-arms reports to the Speaker) did not approve pre-positioning, citing concerns including “optics.” Pelosi’s office has said she was not informed of the request in advance. DoD had offered support earlier; it was not taken up by Capitol security officials. Sund has publicly criticized the process and the chain above him.
During the riot: Once the Capitol was breached (roughly 2 p.m.), urgent requests went out. The House sergeant-at-arms sought Pelosi’s staff’s approval around 1:40 p.m.; she approved minutes later. Pelosi, Schumer, and others then pressed Pentagon officials (Acting Defense Secretary Chris Miller, Army Secretary Ryan McCarthy) and others. There was a multi-hour delay at the DoD level. Miller gave key verbal approvals around 3–4:30 p.m.; the first D.C. National Guard troops arrived around 5:40 p.m., after much of the violence had subsided. Footage shot by Pelosi’s daughter shows her and colleagues frustrated by the slow response, questioning why the Guard had not been pre-positioned, and (in places) acknowledging responsibility for preparedness.
Trump’s role: There is no contemporaneous record of a formal Trump order for 10,000–20,000 troops that Pelosi rejected. He made an offhand comment to Miller about needing a large number; Miller treated it as hyperbolic and noted law enforcement believed they had adequate resources. Multiple accounts and testimony indicate Trump did not place calls to military leaders that afternoon to accelerate the response (Pence and others were more active). Some contemporaneous reporting described initial resistance from Trump. Miller has testified he had prior direction to do what was necessary and approved requests without further White House consultation that day.

The multi-hour lag in getting Guard troops to the Capitol was real and involved slow decision-making by the Capitol Police Board beforehand and the Pentagon during the attack. Pelosi’s “we begged Trump for three hours and he savored it” version collapses those institutional failures into a single personal villain narrative. It is political rhetoric, not a precise description of the chain of command or the timeline. Both sides have spent years pushing simplified versions that minimize their own side’s role in the security breakdown.

Secret 1: The Wishlist Drop. The automated host discount and the algorithm's panic button.

She said this is the baseline, the mistake most travelers make because they assume the listed price is the final price. And it almost never is.

"A listing price, like $250 a night, is just the host's starting point. No negotiation. No algorithmic drop. This is the highest retail price the host hopes a desperate tourist will pay."

"But the platform's backend is designed to panic if a user shows interest but doesn't convert. Hosts rely on conversion metrics. So the platform built an automated tool for us."

"If you search, heart a property to add it to your wishlist, and immediately close the app, the host gets an alert. The system prompts them to send you an immediate 10 to 20% Special Offer just to close the deal."

"She said most guests book on the first search because they fear losing the house. 'The listed price IS the highest price. The wishlist drop is where the real savings start. Heart 5 houses, close your laptop, and wake up to 5 discounted offers in your inbox.'"

Perma bulls continue to absorb microeconomic headwinds to defend high duration tech valuations, while bears point to excessive leverage, capital constraints, and a potential tail risk event across concentrated themes. High implied volatility creates prime entry points for disciplined capital deployment and short-volatility overlay strategies.

SMH has retraced ~12% from its early October peak, while the  S&P ~2% of ATHs. Given the acute index concentration in AI infrastructure, terminal valuation outcomes over the next 12 to 18 months carry an outsized weight on broader index returns.

Highest weighted comment of the week: AVGO CEO Hock Tan recently articulated what disciplined capital allocators have noted for quarters: corporate AI investment remains heavily speculative, and enterprise Return on Invested Capital remains unquantified. Capital expenditure in AI remains vital, but cash flow accretion will likely remain constrained to highly specialized sub-segments (such as high-bandwidth memory). In a probabilistic distribution of market scenarios, risk management requires decoupling momentum exposure from fundamental cash-flow generators.

With AI concentration being extrodinarily high, we must assign a heavy weight to the outcome over the next 12-18 months. In my view, AI spend is important, but only for certain pockets of the equity market (such as memory). 

In a world of possibilites and probabilities we must remember the future holds no certanties & for market participants we must rememeber to balance our emotions in a market full of emotions. 

Now what everyone likely wants to know- how am I focused on extracting value from this: 
The answer is quite simple, patience & conviction (also a seller of the volatility!!)

GOLD, LEN, & BROs are all positions I have started building positions in.

Gold: Counter to the traditional view that a hawkish or structurally independent Federal Reserve pressures non-yielding assets, gold remains a prime hedge against fiscal dominance. Notably, they demonstrated significant factor outperformance during the 2000–2004 post-tech-bubble rotation, highlighting its resilience during growth-to-value regime shifts.
$BROS : A high-growth drive-thru beverage concept currently impacted by transient commodity input inflation and supply-chain pressures. Unit economics remain attractive, customer demand exhibits low price elasticity, and unit-expansion runway offers sustained top-line growth regardless of broader consumer discretionary deceleration.

text:
$EOSE PSA: I want to offer a voice of reason while some prominent bulls continue posting optimistic price targets and reassurances about tailwinds and improving company performance.

I rode $150k up to $1.5m and back down to $110k. Those were my decisions, and I own them. But part of what kept me holding was the false confidence I drew from the community’s consensus. When enough apparently intelligent people keep reassuring each other, uncertainty starts to feel like certainty.

That reassurance is a dangerous drug.

The tailwinds may be real. The company may be improving. Neither guarantees a good outcome for shareholders, particularly when cash burn, financing and dilution remain part of the picture.

However knowledgeable or convincing someone may be, they cannot tell the future. They are sharing an opinion, often with money invested in the outcome themselves. Community members are not accountable to you for what happens to your portfolio. They do not have to fund your losses or live with the consequences.

Your gains and losses are ultimately yours.

There is still ample room for further downside. Under conservative assumptions about cash burn, financing and dilution, an entry with a margin of safety could sit roughly 50% below current levels. That estimate depends on assumptions, and even reaching it would not establish a floor. If the business deteriorates or financing becomes more punitive, the valuation can fall further and the stock can keep going down.

That is a risk scenario, not a prediction. Eos could recover without reaching those prices. But being down roughly 90% from its 52-week high does not automatically make the remaining downside small or capped.

Question the assumptions, including mine. Decide how much you can afford to lose and what evidence would make you change your mind. Nobody posting a price target can make those decisions for you.

Listen to people, but make your own financial decisions. The comfort of belonging to a community should never replace your judgement.

I wish I had understood that before learning it the expensive way.

This post may not make me popular, and that is fine. My concern is the individual investor sitting alone with losses they cannot stomach, while the timeline keeps telling them everything will be fine.

And if that is you, please speak to someone you trust. You are responsible for your investment decisions, but you do not have to face the emotional consequences alone. No stock or financial loss is worth your life.

Karachi Port and Port Qasim handle the bulk of Pakistan’s seaborne trade and connect investors to markets across the Middle East, Africa, and Central Asia.

He highlighted Sindh’s strong economic base and young workforce, noting that Karachi is Pakistan’s financial capital and home to the State Bank of Pakistan and the Pakistan Stock Exchange. He said Sindh’s population of more than 55 million is young, dynamic, and increasingly skilled.

He also highlighted Sindh’s abundant natural resources, saying that Thar holds about 175 billion tons of lignite, one of the largest coal reserves in the world. He added that “we produce rice, cotton, wheat, sugarcane, fruits, and dates for Pakistan and the world.”

He said, “We have an investor-friendly framework. Special economic zones offer incentives guaranteed by law, including a 10-year income tax exemption and duty-free import of capital goods.”

He said Sindh was the first province in Pakistan to enact the public-private partnership law. Sindh was also one of only two provinces that were ranked alongside sovereign countries. At that time, China was ranked third, while Sindh, Pakistan, was ranked sixth, ahead of many countries in the region.

Goddess Kali on a Nagapattinam Copper Stuiver Coin

In the spirit of Navratri, a copper coin from Nagapattinam bearing the facing figure of Goddess Kali offers a fascinating connection between India's numismatic heritage and its enduring traditions of goddess worship.

Nagapattinam, situated on the southeastern coast of Tamil Nadu along the Bay of Bengal, has a history closely associated with maritime trade, religious exchange, and the cultural development of southern India. Its strategic coastal location made it an important link between the fertile Kaveri delta and overseas trading networks connecting Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia.

text:
Trump Destroyed All Our Futures!

WAIT, WHAT? Part Thirteen: Does Somebody Have a Crystal Ball?

I thought that last accusation was a doozy, but this one may just eclipse that one.

Apparently, Trump has managed to destroy something that hasn't even happened yet.

Now that's something!

I’ve been sitting here scratching my head wondering, how can two people look at the same president, hear the same words, watch the same actions, and see two completely different futures? Actually, I’ve been wondering about that for a long time now.

I look at Trump's vision for America and see hope. Others apparently see disaster.

I see a president who wants peace through strength. Others see someone looking for confrontation and war.

I see a vision of better health, prosperity, and opportunity. Others see policies they believe will harm our health, economy, and environment.

I see someone who wants fairness in women's sports, opportunities for women and minorities, and a country where people can succeed standing on their own two feet. Others see discrimination and hatred.

I see a president who wants America to succeed. A country that produces its own energy, protects its innovations, and can stand up to powerful nations like China. A country strong enough to cooperate with others without sacrificing its own interests.

And I want America to remain America. A nation governed by its Constitution, where freedom of speech, religion, and individual liberty are protected. Where neither political ideology nor religious doctrine takes precedence over our constitutional freedoms.

I don't want to see America abandon those principles in favor of socialism, communism, or religious authoritarianism. I don't want people coming here expecting America to abandon its laws and freedoms to accommodate the political or religious systems they left behind.

I want assimilation and peaceful coexistence, where we respect one another's right to live according to our beliefs without trampling on someone else's freedoms. And I believe Trump wants that, too.

Others look at some of those same goals and worry about isolationism, discrimination, and the erosion of democracy.

Same president. Same policies. Two completely different visions of America's future.

I believe Trump wants a brighter future for this country. I really do. I believe the direction he's trying to take us offers a path toward peace, prosperity, and renewed strength. And yes, I worry about what happens if we abandon the principles that made America successful in the first place.

But here's the thing.

What I believe about the future is still a belief. What someone else fears about the future is still a fear.

And what is fear anyway? It has various acronyms:

F.E.A.R. False Evidence Appearing Real
F.E.A.R. Fear Everything And Run
F.E.A.R. Face Everything And Rise

One is believing something without questioning it. One is running from what you believe. And one is facing it head-on.

Pick one.

We can examine policies, question decisions, and debate their likely consequences. We can look at what has happened and what might happen. But predictions aren't facts, fears aren't guarantees, and neither is optimism.

Still, I’ll choose optimism over fear every day.

I don't know exactly what America's future holds. Neither does Donald Trump. And neither does the person who created the meme that started this series. But I do know this:

Our future isn't something one president owns. It's something all of us have a hand in creating. I don’t believe it’s set in stone. I feel that life is fluid and you get out of it what you put into it, both physically and energetically. And I believe you receive what you dwell on. Whether that is positive or negative is up to you.

So instead of declaring the future is destroyed before it even gets here, shouldn't we be asking what we're doing to make it better?

text:
Cambodia: A Sophisticated Southeast Asian Adventure

Cambodia is one of Southeast Asia's most rewarding destinations, combining world-class ancient monuments, fascinating history, warm hospitality, tropical islands, and surprisingly affordable luxury. While often overshadowed by neighboring Thailand and Vietnam, many experienced travelers consider Cambodia one of the region's most authentic and emotionally impactful countries.

Who Is Cambodia Best For?
Adults and Couples: Excellent Choice

Cambodia is particularly well-suited for:

Cultural and history enthusiasts
Luxury travelers seeking value
Honeymooners
Photography lovers
Food and culinary travelers
Adventure travelers
River cruise guests
Retirees and empty nesters

The combination of luxury hotels, temple exploration, fine dining, wellness experiences, and cultural immersion makes Cambodia an outstanding couples' destination.

Families with Children: Good, But Age Matters

Families can absolutely enjoy Cambodia, especially if children are:

Age 8 and older
Interested in history and exploration
Comfortable with tropical climates

Family-friendly highlights include:

Angkor Wat treasure-hunt style tours
Floating villages on Tonlé Sap Lake
Elephant sanctuaries
Beaches on Koh Rong Island
Ziplining and cycling adventures

However, very young children may find extensive temple touring tiring due to heat and walking distances.

Overall Verdict: Cambodia primarily appeals to adults and culturally curious families rather than families seeking theme parks or resort-style vacations.

Brief History

Cambodia was the heart of the powerful Khmer Empire, which dominated much of Southeast Asia from the 9th through 15th centuries.

The empire's crowning achievement was Angkor, once among the world's largest cities and home to the spectacular Angkor Wat temple complex.

Modern Cambodia also carries the memory of one of the twentieth century's great tragedies. During the Khmer Rouge regime (1975-1979), approximately 1.5 to 2 million Cambodians died through execution, starvation, and forced labor. The country's remarkable recovery and resilience are part of what makes visiting so meaningful.

Today Cambodia is a rapidly developing constitutional monarchy led by King Norodom Sihamoni.

The Cambodian People

Cambodians are widely regarded as among the friendliest people in Southeast Asia.

Visitors often notice:

Genuine warmth
Humility
Strong family values
Deep Buddhist traditions
Resilience despite difficult history

Approximately 95% of the population practices Theravada Buddhism, which strongly influences daily life, festivals, architecture, and social customs.

Cambodian Culture

Cambodian culture is distinctly Khmer.

Highlights include:

Buddhism

Golden temples and saffron-robed monks are common throughout the country.

Traditional Dance

The Royal Ballet of Cambodia features graceful Apsara dancers whose movements are inspired by carvings at Angkor Wat.

Festivals

Major celebrations include:

Khmer New Year (April)
Water Festival (November)
Pchum Ben Ancestor Festival
Arts and Handicrafts

Cambodia is known for:

Silk weaving
Wood carving
Silverwork
Stone sculpture
Cambodian Cuisine

Cambodian cuisine is often overlooked, but it is one of Southeast Asia's hidden culinary treasures.

Popular dishes include:

Amok Trey

Cambodia's national dish.

Fish steamed in coconut curry and banana leaves.

Lok Lak

Stir-fried beef served with lime-pepper dipping sauce.

Kuy Teav

A flavorful noodle soup often eaten for breakfast.

Fresh Seafood

Especially along Cambodia's coast and islands.

Kampot Pepper

Among the world's most celebrated pepper varieties and a favorite among international chefs.

What Makes Cambodia Unique?

Several things distinguish Cambodia from other Asian destinations:

Angkor Wat

The largest religious monument on Earth.

Affordability of Luxury

World-class luxury costs substantially less than equivalent experiences in Thailand, Singapore, or Japan.

Authenticity

Many destinations remain uncrowded compared to neighboring countries.

Emotional Impact

Visitors can experience both the grandeur of Angkor and learn about Cambodia's modern history, creating a powerful travel experience.

Tonlé Sap Lake

One of the world's most unusual freshwater ecosystems, with a river that reverses direction seasonally.

Top 3 Must-Do Experiences
1. Explore Angkor Wat and Angkor Archaeological Park

This is Cambodia's defining experience.

Must-see temples:

Angkor Wat
Bayon
Ta Prohm
Banteay Srei

Allow:

2 to 3 full days minimum

Many luxury travelers hire private guides and photographers.

2. Experience Tonlé Sap Lake and Floating Villages

See entire communities living on water.

Highlights include:

Floating homes
Schools
Markets
Bird sanctuaries

This provides remarkable insight into traditional Cambodian life.

3. Stay at a Luxury Resort and Experience Khmer Hospitality

Unlike many countries where luxury can feel internationalized, Cambodia's best hotels embrace Khmer culture.

Luxury travelers frequently rank Cambodian service among the best in Asia. Luxury hotels commonly range from about $150-$400 per night, with premier properties often higher.

Best Time to Visit

The most comfortable season is generally November through February, when conditions are drier and temperatures are relatively moderate. Cambodia's dry season typically runs from November through April, while the wet season runs from May through October.

Best Months
November
December
January
February
Shoulder Season Value
Late October
Early November
March
Avoid If Possible
April (extreme heat)
September (heaviest rainfall)
How Far in Advance Should You Book?
Standard Upscale Travel
4 to 6 months ahead
Luxury Travel
6 to 9 months ahead
Peak Holiday Travel

Christmas, New Year, and Lunar New Year:

9 to 12 months ahead

The most desirable luxury properties around Angkor Wat can fill surprisingly early during peak season.

Estimated Airfare from the Continental United States

Most flights connect through:

Singapore
Seoul
Tokyo
Taipei
Hong Kong
Doha

Typical round-trip prices per person:

Cabin Average FareEconomy $800 - $1,500
Premium Economy $1,600 - $2,800
Business Class $4,000 - $7,500+
First Class (limited routes) $8,000 - $15,000+

Recent searches show economy fares from roughly $575-$1,200+ round trip depending on city and season, while business-class itineraries commonly start around $4,000 from major U.S. gateways.

Typical Luxury Vacation Cost

Assuming a 10-day trip.

Couple: Upscale

Hotels:

$200-$400/night

Trip Cost:

$5,500-$8,500 total

Includes:

Economy airfare
Quality hotels
Private tours
Some fine dining
Couple: Luxury

Hotels:

$500-$1,000+/night

Trip Cost:

$10,000-$18,000 total

Includes:

Luxury resorts
Private guides
Premium dining
Internal transfers

Business-class airfare can push total trip costs above $20,000.

Family of 4: Upscale

Hotels:

Two rooms or family suite

Trip Cost:

$8,500-$13,000 total

Includes:

Economy flights
Upscale accommodations
Private family tours
Comfortable transportation
Family of 4: Luxury

Hotels:

Luxury family suite or villa

Trip Cost:

$15,000-$30,000+

Includes:

High-end hotels
Private guides and drivers
Luxury experiences
Premium dining

Business-class flights for four can add $16,000-$30,000 or more to the total budget.

Bottom Line

For travelers from the United States, Cambodia is one of the world's best values in luxury travel. It offers a combination that few destinations can match:

One of humanity's greatest archaeological wonders
Outstanding luxury hotels
Rich Buddhist culture
Warm and welcoming people
Excellent cuisine
Fascinating history
Relatively affordable pricing

For most American travelers, I would recommend 10-12 days between Siem Reap, Phnom Penh, and either the Cambodian coast or a luxury nature lodge, ideally between November and February for the best overall experience.

text:
Warriors For Christ Ministries

THE GOSPEL WALK
Matthew — Chapter 4 of 28

EXPLAINED
Matthew 4 opens with Jesus led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil. After forty days and nights of fasting, He is hungry. The tempter comes with three offers: turn stones into bread, cast Himself down from the temple pinnacle so angels will catch Him, and receive all the kingdoms of the world in exchange for worship. Each time Jesus answers with the written Word: “It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God” (Matthew 4:4, KJV); “Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God” (Matthew 4:7, KJV); and “Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve” (Matthew 4:10, KJV). The devil leaves, and angels come and minister unto Him.

When Jesus hears that John the Baptist has been cast into prison, He departs into Galilee, leaves Nazareth, and dwells in Capernaum by the sea, fulfilling the prophecy of Isaiah that light has come to Galilee of the Gentiles. From that time He begins to preach, saying, “Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand” (Matthew 4:17, KJV). Walking by the sea of Galilee, He calls Simon called Peter and Andrew his brother, then James and John the sons of Zebedee, saying, “Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men” (Matthew 4:19, KJV). They immediately leave their nets and their father and follow Him. Jesus then goes about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and disease among the people, so that great multitudes follow Him from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judaea, and beyond Jordan.

SUMMARY
Matthew 4 shows Jesus overcoming the devil’s temptations by the Word of God, then launching His public ministry in Galilee with the call to repent, the calling of the first disciples, and the demonstration of kingdom power through teaching, preaching, and healing.

KEY POINTS
- The Holy Spirit leads Jesus into the wilderness for the purpose of being tempted, and Jesus meets every temptation with Scripture.
- After the victory, angels minister to Him, and He moves into Galilee when He hears of John’s imprisonment.
- His message is clear and urgent: “Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.”
- He calls ordinary fishermen—Peter, Andrew, James, and John—and they immediately leave everything to follow Him.
- His ministry combines teaching in the synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every kind of sickness.
- Multitudes from surrounding regions follow Him because of the power and authority of His word and works.
- The chapter establishes both the pattern of resisting the enemy with the Word and the pattern of calling disciples into kingdom labor.

APPLY IT TODAY
When temptation presses, answer it the way Jesus did—with the written Word of God, not with your own reasoning or appetite. Then walk in the same call He gave His disciples: repent, follow Him, and let Him turn your ordinary life into a means of gathering others. Teaching the truth, proclaiming the kingdom, and showing compassion through acts of mercy still mark the path of those who follow the King.

VERSES THAT GO WITH IT
- Deuteronomy 8:3
- Deuteronomy 6:16
- Deuteronomy 6:13
- Isaiah 9:1-2
- Mark 1:15
- Luke 5:10-11
- Acts 2:38

text:
When my kids throw a tantrum my first instinct is to offer them honey and some water. It immediately calms them and gives them a bit of clarity. If they accept it, the next thing i offer is a hug, it makes them feel safe and the hostility subsides. But sometimes when they’re being unreasonable and refuse the honey, refuse to listen. I just sit down near my child and let them get all the yelling and screaming out. Sometimes you just need to let it out, i get it. 

What i never do is leave them isolated when theyre crying, screaming, having a meltdown. At times like that theyre unwilling to accept anything so i acknowledge their feelings simply with my presence. I do not want them to feel like when theyre being difficult they deserve to be abandoned. I want them to realise that its ok to have big feelings. Theyre too little to be able to process things efficiently. Expecting things from children that we as adults fail to apply is simply unfair. After they’re done i again offer the honey and most of the time they accept it and then theyre ready for a hug too. Children need infinite grace and patience. 

I think a lot of friction that comes into parenting is because of the ‘karta bhav’ in the parent. Parents think im the person responsible for this childs destiny but that is a lie. We only have been given a responsibility to nourish and guide the children. We cannot decide their fate because we do not own them. We cannot own other humans not even if we birthed them painstakingly. This sense of ownership ruins any relationship. When we wanted a child, my husband and i wanted a son to be the elder child. So a little baby girl does not have to deal with intensity of the responsibility that comes with being an elder child. 

We went to our ishta’s temple. And we both humbly prayed to him. We told him you know what our home is like, what our family is like. What kind of parents we will be. Everything is known to you. We requested him to place a soul into our home, a soul that is his bhakta, we promised him that we would both try our very best to protect and guide the child. And that the baby would always remain as if offered at his feet. Whatever destiny he would choose to write for our child, we will accept it as his grace on us. And then our son was conceived. Hes a wonderful, intelligent, humble little boy. For our girls too we had prayed to our Swamini to bless us with a babygirl and she gave us two.

Now when we raise them, we do not see it from a lens of ownership. Its purely stewardship. Because it is only a gentle soul placed in our care. It is all Bhagwan’s leela that we get to be a part of. Raising souls that are dear to him, providing a safe, loving shelter to them, this has always been our only intention with expanding our family. Everything falls in place when you connect everything to Bhagwan. Because the infinite grace required only has its source from him, nowhere else is it found. Pouring from an empty cup is impossible.

Varaahi Homam Poornahuthi of today Panchami tithi Navaratri 🪷

We are very fortunate that Sri TM Narayan Namboodiri the previous Melshanti of Guruvayoorappan Temple Kerala visited us today here at Seeta Rama Kovil, Mumbai. Sri Namboodiri being honoured by our temple president.

This is a very powerful Homam that invokes Devi Vaarahi, the consort & Shakti of Shri Varaha Swamy Himself. She is Bhoodevi or Dharani Herself and is one among the Sapta Maatrikas.

Red coloured Saree, red coloured flowers or fruits should be offered to Devi Vaarahi. Today a beautiful red coloured Saree was offered to Devi in the Poornahuthi.

Sri Shweta Varaha Swamy is the Lord of our current Kalpa called 'Shweta Varaha Kalpa'. Hence, He & Devi Vaarahi must be worshipped by each of us in every Pooje, Homam, Aaradhane or any Mangalakaarya that we perform.

Devi Vaarahi destroys all negativity, enemies and evil forces & grants immense protection to Her devotee.
Also this Homam grants excellent health, prosperity, success in career and a long fulfilling life to the devotee.
